```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("BravoPadros_2026_odronextamab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("BravoPadros_2026_odronextamab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70162> (open access; Appendix S1
  holds the NONMEM control stream of the fit-for-purpose model and the
  supplementary tables and figures)

Odronextamab is a CD20xCD3 bispecific IgG4 T-cell-engaging antibody.
Bravo Padros 2026 pooled 14,618 serum concentrations from 507 adults with
relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (B-NHL) in the Phase I
ELM-1 and Phase II ELM-2 studies, dosed IV from 0.03 to 320 mg.

Structure (Equations 1-3): a two-compartment model with parallel linear
and Michaelis-Menten elimination from the central compartment. The
maximum velocity of the Michaelis-Menten (target-mediated) pathway
declines over time toward an asymptote, which the authors relate to
treatment-induced B-cell depletion:

\[
\frac{dV_{\max}}{dt} = -K_v\, V_{\max}\left(1 - \frac{V_{\max,\mathrm{asym}}}{V_{\max}}\right),
\qquad V_{\max}(0) = V_{\max,0}, \qquad V_{\max,\mathrm{asym}} = R_v\, V_{\max,0}
\]

which the packaged model uses in closed form,
\(V_{\max}(t) = V_{\max,0}\,[R_v + (1 - R_v)\,e^{-K_v t}]\), with
\(t\) the time since the first dose. The Michaelis-Menten elimination
rate constant is \(K_{MM} = V_{\max}(t) / (k_m + C)\).

The model reports three parameterisations (base, full, and
fit-for-purpose); the fit-for-purpose model is the one the authors used
for all simulations and is the one packaged here.

# Population

Table 1: 507 patients (ELM-1 n = 167, ELM-2 n = 340). Histology: DLBCL
CAR T naive 39.8%, DLBCL after CAR T failure 11.6%, follicular lymphoma
(FL) 32.7%, mantle cell lymphoma 4.9%, marginal zone lymphoma 4.9%,
other B-NHL 5.9%. Median age 65 years (IQR 55-72), body weight 72.6 kg
(IQR 61.4-84.0), 38.3% female, 62% White, Ann Arbor stage IV 61.5%,
prior CAR T therapy 13.0%. Median baseline albumin 38.7 g/L, IgG
38.2 umol/L, lymphocytes 0.792 x 10^9/L, IL-10 3.02 ng/L, IFN gamma
3.66 ng/L and tumour size (sum of products of perpendicular diameters)
2930 mm^2.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("BravoPadros_2026_odronextamab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/BravoPadros_2026_odronextamab.R`. Final
estimates come from Table 2 (fit-for-purpose column); equation forms and
reference covariate values come from the Appendix S1 control stream,
whose `$THETA` / `$OMEGA` blocks carry initial estimates from an earlier
run and are not used for values.

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL) | log(0.189 L/day) | Table 2 |
| `lq` (Q) | log(1.21 L/day) | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (Vc) | log(4.99 L) | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (Vp) | log(4.42 L) | Table 2 |
| `lvmax` (Vmax,0) | log(2.93 mg/L/day) | Table 2 |
| `lkm` (km) | log(1.95 mg/L) | Table 2 |
| `lvmax_exp_kdes` (Kv) | log(1.09 1/day) | Table 2 |
| `lvmax_exp_finf` (Rv) | log(0.262) | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.854 | Table 2 |
| `e_alb_cl` (time-varying albumin) | -0.933 | Table 2 |
| `e_igg_cl` | 0.118 | Table 2 |
| `e_ifng_cl` | 0.0274 | Table 2 |
| `e_il10_cl` | -0.0717 | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 0.372 | Table 2 |
| `e_alb_base_vc_vp` | -0.561 | Table 2 |
| `e_sexf_vc_vp` | -0.186 | Table 2 |
| `e_lymph_abs_vc_vp` | 0.0895 | Table 2 |
| `e_ann_arbor_lt4_vmax` | -0.285 | Table 2 |
| `e_lymph_abs_vmax` | 0.313 | Table 2 |
| `e_tumtp_fl_vmax` | -0.252 | Table 2 |
| `e_prior_cart_vmax` | -0.201 | Table 2 |
| `e_tumsz_vmax` | 0.0601 | Table 2 |
| `e_tumtp_fl_vmax_exp_kdes`, `e_tumtp_other_nhl_vmax_exp_kdes` | -0.891, -0.844 | Table 2 |
| `e_tumtp_fl_vmax_exp_finf`, `e_tumtp_other_nhl_vmax_exp_finf` | -0.133, -0.292 | Table 2 |
| `etalvc`, `etalvmax`, `etalvp` (variances) | 0.0983, 0.403, 0.709 | Table 2 |
| `expSd` | sqrt(0.136) | Table 2 (residual variance, ln mg/L) |
| Reference covariates (72.6 kg, 38.7 g/L, 38.2 umol/L, 3.01 and 3.66 ng/L, 0.792 x 10^9/L, 2930 mm^2) | -- | Appendix S1 `$PK` (`MED_*`); Table 2 footnote |
| Power forms `(cov / median)^theta`; `(1 + theta)` forms for categorical effects | -- | Appendix S1 `$PK` |
| One covariate factor shared by Vc and Vp (`COV_V`) | -- | Appendix S1 `$PK` |
| Two-compartment ODEs with \(K_{MM} = V_{\max} / (k_m + C)\) | -- | Equations 1-2; Appendix S1 `$DES` |
| Vmax time course | -- | Equation 3; Appendix S1 `$DES` `DADT(3)` |
| Residual error additive on log concentration | -- | Appendix S1 `$ERROR` |

# Dosing regimen and virtual cohort

The simulations follow the 0.7/4/20/160 mg QW / 320 mg Q2W regimen of
Table 3 and Figure 3: step-up doses of 0.7, 4 and 20 mg in weeks 1-3,
160 mg QW to week 12, then 320 mg Q2W. All doses are 1-h infusions.
Steady state is evaluated over weeks 42-43 (days 294-308), as in the
paper.

The observed data are not public. A virtual cohort of 200 patients is
drawn from the Table 1 marginal summaries: continuous covariates are
log-normal (albumin normal) with the published median and a spread set
from the interquartile range, truncated to the extreme quantile bins of
Table 3; histology, sex, Ann Arbor stage and prior CAR T therapy follow
the Table 1 proportions (prior CAR T only within DLBCL). Albumin is held
at its baseline value over time (`ALB = ALB_BASE`).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_sub <- 200

# log-normal draw from a median and an interquartile range, truncated
draw_ln <- function(n, med, q1, q3, lo, hi) {
  pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n, log(med), log(q3 / q1) / 1.349), lo), hi)
}

hist_p <- c(
  "DLBCL, CAR T naive" = 0.398, "DLBCL, CAR T failure" = 0.116,
  "FL" = 0.327, "Other B-NHL" = 0.159
)
alb <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 38.7, (42 - 34) / 1.349), 16), 56)
subjects <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  histology = sample(names(hist_p), n_sub, replace = TRUE, prob = hist_p),
  WT = draw_ln(n_sub, 72.6, 61.4, 84.0, 31.8, 165),
  ALB_BASE = alb,
  ALB = alb,
  # Table 1 IgG is in umol/L; the model column is g/L (150 kDa)
  IGG = draw_ln(n_sub, 38.2, 25.4, 53.8, 4.07, 300) * 0.15,
  # Table 1 lymphocytes are 10^9/L; the model column is cells/uL
  LYMPH_ABS = draw_ln(n_sub, 0.792, 0.49, 1.30, 0.03, 44.3) * 1000,
  IL10 = draw_ln(n_sub, 3.02, 0.93, 11.0, 0.6, 9750),
  IFNG = draw_ln(n_sub, 3.66, 1.68, 12.1, 0.022, 2040),
  TUMSZ = draw_ln(n_sub, 2930, 1480, 5220, 75, 46100),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.383),
  ANN_ARBOR_LT4 = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 1 - 0.615)
) |>
  mutate(
    PRIOR_CART = as.integer(histology == "DLBCL, CAR T failure"),
    TUMTP_FL = as.integer(histology == "FL"),
    TUMTP_OTHER_NHL = as.integer(histology == "Other B-NHL"),
    sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "Female", "Male")
  )

dose_tab <- tibble(
  time = c(0, 7, 14, seq(21, 77, by = 7), seq(84, 294, by = 14)),
  amt = c(0.7, 4, 20, rep(160, 9), rep(320, 16))
)
stopifnot(max(dose_tab$time) == 294, sum(dose_tab$amt == 160) == 9)
inf_dur <- 1 / 24

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 21, by = 0.5),
  seq(21, 28, by = 0.125), 21 + inf_dur,
  seq(28, 77, by = 1),
  seq(77, 84, by = 0.125), 77 + inf_dur,
  seq(84, 294, by = 2),
  seq(294, 308, by = 0.125), 294 + inf_dur
)))

make_events <- function(subj) {
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(subj, dose_tab) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, dur = inf_dur, cmt = "central")
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, evid, amt, dur, cmt, everything()) |>
    as.data.frame()
}
events <- make_events(subjects)
```

# Simulation

Table 3 summarises individual predictions from post hoc parameter
estimates, so the comparison uses the simulated individual prediction
`Cc` (between-subject variability included, residual error excluded).

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("BravoPadros_2026_odronextamab")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("histology", "sex"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc), all(sim$Cc >= 0))
```

## Concentration-time profiles

```{r profile-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (week)",
    y = "Odronextamab concentration (mg/L)",
    title = "0.7/4/20/160 mg QW / 320 mg Q2W: median and 90% interval",
    caption = "Individual predictions of 200 virtual patients (compare Figure S4)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Time course of Vmax by histology

Replicates Figure 4E of Bravo Padros 2026 for the typical DLBCL and FL
patient: the Michaelis-Menten Vmax falls toward its asymptote within the
first weeks of treatment, faster in DLBCL than in FL (Kv 1.09 vs.
0.119 1/day).

```{r vmax-time, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
# Typical-value solves of several patients at once; rxode2 warns that no
# omega is left after zeroRe(), which is the intent here.
solve_typ <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
ref_pat <- tibble(
  WT = 72.6, ALB_BASE = 38.7, ALB = 38.7, IGG = 38.2 * 0.15,
  LYMPH_ABS = 792, IL10 = 3.01, IFNG = 3.66, TUMSZ = 2930,
  SEXF = 0, ANN_ARBOR_LT4 = 0, PRIOR_CART = 0, TUMTP_FL = 0, TUMTP_OTHER_NHL = 0
)
typ_hist <- bind_rows(
  ref_pat |> mutate(id = 1L, histology = "DLBCL"),
  ref_pat |> mutate(id = 2L, histology = "FL", TUMTP_FL = 1)
)
sim_hist <- solve_typ(
  events = make_events(typ_hist) |> filter(time <= 63),
  keep = "histology",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
ggplot(sim_hist, aes(time / 7, vmax_t, colour = histology)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (week)",
    y = "Vmax (mg/L/day)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical reference patient; replicates Figure 4E."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# Closed form of Equation 3 against its own definition: at day 63 Vmax has
# reached Rv * Vmax,0 for DLBCL (0.262 * 2.93) and for FL
# (0.262 * 0.867 * 2.93 * 0.748).
v63 <- sim_hist |> filter(time == 63)
stopifnot(
  abs(v63$vmax_t[v63$histology == "DLBCL"] / (0.262 * 2.93) - 1) < 1e-3,
  abs(v63$vmax_t[v63$histology == "FL"] / (0.262 * (1 - 0.133) * 2.93 * (1 - 0.252)) - 1) < 0.01
)
```

The figure uses the typical DLBCL and FL patients. In FL the decline is
about nine-fold slower (Kv reduced by 89.1%), which is why FL patients
have lower exposure than DLBCL patients during the step-up weeks
(Figure 4A-D).

## Michaelis-Menten clearance at baseline and at the asymptote

The paper reports a median modified Michaelis-Menten clearance
\(CL_{MM} = K_{MM} V_c\) of 5.43 L/day (DLBCL) and 4.67 L/day (FL) at
baseline, and 0.0296 and 0.025 L/day at the asymptote. The table gives
the same summaries for the virtual cohort: at time 0 (no drug present)
and at the steady-state trough.

```{r clmm}
clmm <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 308), histology != "Other B-NHL") |>
  mutate(
    hist2 = ifelse(histology == "FL", "FL", "DLBCL"),
    clmm = kel_mm * vc,
    when = ifelse(time == 0, "Baseline", "Steady-state trough")
  ) |>
  group_by(hist2, when) |>
  summarise(sim_median = format(signif(median(clmm), 3)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(paper = c(5.43, 0.0296, 4.67, 0.025))
clmm |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Histology = hist2, Time = when,
    "Simulated median CLMM (L/day)" = sim_median,
    "Paper median CLMM (L/day)" = paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median Michaelis-Menten clearance, virtual cohort vs. Results text.")
```

The paper does not say at which time or concentration its asymptotic
CLMM was computed; at the steady-state trough the saturable pathway is
almost fully saturated (concentrations of about 85 mg/L against a km
of 1.95 mg/L), so CLMM is close to zero either way. The simulated
medians lie within about 15% of the reported ones, which come from the
post hoc estimates of the real patients.

# PKNCA: steady-state exposure (Table 3) and accumulation

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(regimen = "0.7/4/20/160 mg QW / 320 mg Q2W") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen, sex)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(regimen = "0.7/4/20/160 mg QW / 320 mg Q2W") |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen, sex)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + sex + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "day")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + sex + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(21, 77, 294),
  end = c(28, 84, 308),
  auclast = TRUE,
  cmax = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE),
  cmin = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)
```

Steady-state Cmin, Cmax and AUC over the dosing interval at weeks 42-43,
overall and by sex, against the Table 3 medians:

```{r nca-compare}
ss <- nca_res |> filter(start == 294, PPTESTCD %in% c("cmin", "cmax", "auclast"))
ss_sim <- bind_rows(
  ss |> mutate(subgroup = "Overall"),
  ss |> mutate(subgroup = sex)
) |>
  select(subgroup, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

# Table 3, median steady-state exposure (0.7/4/20/160 mg QW / 320 mg Q2W)
ss_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~subgroup, ~cmin, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "Overall", 84.6, 156, 1470,
  "Female", 99.8, 189, 1750,
  "Male", 76.5, 141, 1350
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = ss_sim,
  reference = ss_ref,
  by = "subgroup",
  units = c(cmin = "mg/L", cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "day*mg/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. Table 3 median steady-state exposure (weeks 42-43).")
if (!is.null(attr(cmp, "footnote"))) cat(attr(cmp, "footnote"))

pct <- ss_sim |>
  group_by(subgroup, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(ss_ref, -subgroup, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("subgroup", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / ref - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(pct) == 9L)
# Assert on the overall medians only: the by-sex rows depend on the
# weight-sex correlation, which the independent covariate draws do not
# carry (see below). A mis-transcribed CL, volume or unit moves the
# overall medians by tens of percent.
pct_overall <- pct |> filter(subgroup == "Overall")
stopifnot(abs(median(pct_overall$pct_diff)) < 10)
```

The overall steady-state medians agree within about 5%. The female and
male rows are closer together than in Table 3, because the
model's sex effect acts only on the volumes; most of the exposure
difference between the sexes in the real data comes from the lower body
weight of the women, and the virtual cohort draws weight independently
of sex.

Accumulation of the full 160 mg QW dose, as the ratio of the AUC over
week 12 (days 77-84) to the AUC over week 4 (days 21-28, the first
160 mg dose); the paper reports a median of 3.87 (IQR 3.56-4.25):

```{r accumulation}
acc <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", start %in% c(21, 77)) |>
  select(id, start, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = start, values_from = PPORRES, names_prefix = "auc_") |>
  mutate(ratio = auc_77 / auc_21)
acc_q <- quantile(acc$ratio, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
knitr::kable(
  tibble(
    Statistic = c("Q1", "Median", "Q3"),
    Simulated = signif(unname(acc_q), 3),
    Paper = c(3.56, 3.87, 4.25)
  ),
  caption = "Accumulation ratio AUC(week 12) / AUC(week 4), 160 mg QW."
)
stopifnot(abs(acc_q[["50%"]] / 3.87 - 1) < 0.15)
```

The ratio combines accumulation from the roughly five-week terminal
half-life with the decline in target-mediated clearance between weeks 4
and 12, so it exercises both the linear and the time-varying parts of
the model.

# Marginal covariate effects on steady-state Cmin (Figure 3C)

Figure 3 varies one covariate at a time from the reference patient
(fixed effects only) and reports the fold change in steady-state Cmin;
the Results text quotes body weight, albumin and IL-10. Albumin is
changed in both the baseline (volume) and the time-varying (CL) column.

```{r marginal}
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~cov, ~value, ~paper,
  "Reference", "none", NA, 1,
  "Weight 49.8 kg", "WT", 49.8, 1.47,
  "Weight 111 kg", "WT", 111, 0.632,
  "Albumin 28.3 g/L", "ALB", 28.3, 0.689,
  "Albumin 46 g/L", "ALB", 46, 1.22,
  "IL-10 0.6 ng/L", "IL10", 0.6, 0.871,
  "IL-10 79 ng/L", "IL10", 79, 1.30
)
marg_subj <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  p <- ref_pat |> mutate(id = i, scenario = scen$scenario[i])
  if (scen$cov[i] == "WT") p$WT <- scen$value[i]
  if (scen$cov[i] == "ALB") {
    p$ALB <- scen$value[i]
    p$ALB_BASE <- scen$value[i]
  }
  if (scen$cov[i] == "IL10") p$IL10 <- scen$value[i]
  p
}))
sim_marg <- solve_typ(
  events = make_events(marg_subj),
  keep = "scenario",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
marg <- sim_marg |>
  filter(time >= 294, time <= 308) |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(cmin = min(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(fold = cmin / cmin[scenario == "Reference"]) |>
  inner_join(scen, by = "scenario") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (fold / paper - 1))
marg |>
  arrange(match(scenario, scen$scenario)) |>
  transmute(
    Scenario = scenario,
    "Simulated fold change" = signif(fold, 3),
    "Paper fold change" = paper,
    "% diff" = round(pct_diff, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fold change in steady-state Cmin relative to the reference patient.")
stopifnot(all(abs(marg$pct_diff) < 5))
```

These are deterministic typical-value predictions, so the tolerance is
tight. The paper's fold changes are medians over simulations with
parameter uncertainty, which explains the small residual differences.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Final estimates.** The `$THETA`, `$OMEGA` and `$SIGMA` blocks of the
  Appendix S1 control stream are labelled as taken from an earlier run
  and differ from Table 2 (e.g. initial Vmax,0 exp(1.02) = 2.77 vs.
  final 2.93 mg/L/day); the packaged values are the Table 2
  fit-for-purpose estimates.
- **Vmax state.** The control stream integrates Vmax as a third ODE
  state starting at Vmax,0. The packaged model uses the exact closed-form
  solution in `t`, so the first dose must be given at time 0.
- **Covariate units.** IgG is a g/L column in the package and is
  converted to umol/L inside the model at an assumed IgG molar mass of
  150 kDa (the paper reports IgG in umol/L without a conversion factor).
  Lymphocytes are a cells/uL column, converted to 10^9/L.
- **Missing covariates.** The source analysis imputed missing baseline
  covariates (5.3% for IL-10 and IFN gamma) with the cohort median.
  Supply the median (3.01 and 3.66 ng/L) for a missing value.
- **Other B-NHL effect on Vmax,0.** The control stream keeps a commented
  effect of MCL/MZL/other B-NHL on Vmax,0, which was dropped from the
  fit-for-purpose model (Results); it is not encoded.
- **Covariates screened but not retained** (age, ALT, race, bulky
  disease, CRP, creatinine clearance and renal function, ECOG, IgG on the
  volumes, IL-2, IL-6, IL-8, TNF alpha, LDH; Methods and Table S3) are not
  part of the model.
- **No variability on CL.** The paper reports that between-subject
  variability on CL could not be estimated; time-varying albumin carries
  part of the CL variability.
- **Dosing details.** The paper does not state infusion durations beyond
  "over 1-4 h" or the exact step-up days; the vignette uses 1-h infusions
  given on the weekly schedule above.
- **Virtual cohort.** Covariates are drawn independently from marginal
  distributions anchored at the Table 1 medians and interquartile ranges;
  the joint covariate structure of the real patients is not reproduced.
  Albumin is held at baseline over time.
